claims.text: Slight non-equiatomic deviations in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles reduce configurational entropy.
Reduced configurational entropy promotes differential atomic mobility during heating.
Heating causes preferential surface segregation of lower-melting-point elements such as Cu.
Cu is a lower-melting-point constituent of the stated alloy system.
Surface enrichment in lower-melting-point elements locally lowers the melting point.
The locally lowered melting point initiates a liquid-like surface skin.
The liquid-like surface skin governs the overall premelting and melting behavior.
The starting nanoparticles are single-phase Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu solid solutions.
A thin surface layer enriched in lower-melting-point elements forms during heating.
Formation of the enriched surface layer is correlated with lattice-parameter shifts.
Configurational entropy stabilizes the homogeneous solid solution.
Reduced solid-solution stability upon heating enhances atomic mobility.
A surface-directed chemical gradient triggers surface-initiated premelting.
Non-equiatomic nanoparticles will show an earlier onset of surface disorder and premelting than equiatomic nanoparticles.
Non-equiatomic nanoparticles will form a liquid-like surface skin earlier than equiatomic nanoparticles.
Non-equiatomic nanoparticles will exhibit shifted DSC heat-flow profiles and XRD diffraction peaks relative to equiatomic nanoparticles.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will maintain a more uniform solid solution than modestly non-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Equiatomic nanoparticles will display a sharper and higher-temperature melting transition.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase solid-solution nanoparticles approximately 5–50 nm in size under controlled heating and cooling rates.
Extreme compositional deviations or substantial particle-size anomalies may activate additional phase-transformation mechanisms.
